pr_body:
Add --secondary-sub-delay option and decouple --sub-delay from secondary subtitles. This produces desirable behavior in most cases as secondary and primary subtitles tracks tend to be timed independently of one another.

This feature is implemented by turning the sub_delay field in mp_subtitle_opts into an array of 2 floats. From here the track index is either passed around or derived when sub_delay is needed. There are some cases in dec_sub.c where it is possible for dec_sub.order (equivalent to track index) to be -1. In these cases, sub_delay is inferred as 0.

Closes #2629

---

The pull request contains code for the "ideal" solution as far as I'm concerned, but based on the discussion that happened last time in #8954 I doubt it will be merged as is. This time around I'm interested in finding an amicable solution to the problem.

If breaking backwards compatibility is a concern, implementing a boolean option like `--sync-sub-delays` that guarantees `secondary-sub-delay` is the the same value as `sub-delay` if set to `yes` would allow the existing behavior to exist alongside the new behavior.
pr_comments: Thanks for working on this @ripose-jp! :) This will greatly help my language learning setup!

The [IINA](https://github.com/iina/iina) project has also had requests from users for this feature.

On this:
> If breaking backwards compatibility is a concern, implementing a boolean option like --sync-sub-delays that guarantees secondary-sub-delay is the the same value as sub-delay if set to yes would allow the existing behavior to exist alongside the new behavior.

mpv already has a concept of option values that are keywords or numbers as can be seen in [loop-playlist](https://mpv.io/manual/stable/#options-loop-playlist). So an alternative to having a separate option to synchronize the subtitle delays and preserve backward compatibility would be to have `secondary-sub-delay` be something like:

> **--secondary-sub-delay=<sec | sync>**
    Delays secondary subtitles by ``<sec>`` seconds. Can be negative. If set to `sync` (the default), any delay specified in `--sub-delay` for the primary subtitle will be used for the secondary subtitle as well.

Something like that.

issue_context.title: Different delays when using "--secondary-sub"
issue_context.body:
The feature of showing two subtitles at once is extremely useful when watching films in two languages, because you can simultaneously have the subtitles of your native languages and the subtitles in the language you want to learn.

The problem is that often the subtitles have not the same timing (in relation to the video). When only using one subtitle you can correct this with "sub-delay", but when using two subtitles (with "secondary-sid") this value applies to both files. For example: subtitle 1 is perfectly aligned with the video, but the second subtitle is +10s compared to the video. When using "sub-delay=-10" the second subtitle is now perfect but the first is wrong.

There are be multiple solutions to this problem:

1) "inter-sub-delay"
The delay of the secondary sub is now "sub-delay + inter-sub-delay". So "sub-delay" still influences the second subtitle.

2) "secondary-sub-delay"
The value "sub-delay" does not influence the delay of the second subtitle. Instead there is an independent value called "secondary-sub-delay".

3) per-file-delays
This would be the solution I prefer. Example: in case you have you have three or more subtitles you want to cycle through (this happens sometimes to me). Subtitle 1 can be perfect, subtitle 2 could be "+10s" and subtitle 3 could be "-10s". Because the subtitle for "secondary-sid" can change, using "+10s" or "-10s" for "inter-sub-delay" or "secondary-sub-delay" won't work. It is clear that per-file-delays are needed here.

I would be happy with either of these solutions. This would really simplify playing files without having to edit and re-time the subtitle files (that destroys the formatting of subtitles in some programs).

In case there is already a way around this problem (which was unable to find)  I would be grateful if you can describe it to me.
